summary: Summation No. 30 covers March 1948, the month in which Hitoshi Ashida formed a coalition cabinet of Democrats (six), Social Democrats (eight) and People's Cooperative Party members (two) on the basis of a three-party policy agreement. It reports the new Police Reorganization Law taking effect on 7 March, the founding of the Democratic Liberal Party on 15 March, the reconvened Second Diet and the Prime Minister's policy address, the winding up of the purge screening committees by 10 May, discoveries of hoarded goods, and the defense summation at the International Military Tribunal. The economic sections give February and March statistics on agriculture, mining, heavy industry, textiles, communications, labor disputes (coal, electric power, express transport), trade, rationing, prices, banking and finance, science and technology. Social sections cover communicable disease, public assistance, repatriation, vital statistics, education, religion and the media. Historians will find the detailed cabinet formation narrative, party realignments and production and finance tables especially useful.
highlights: A three-party policy agreement among the Democratic, Social Democratic and People's Cooperative Parties, with concessions to the Social Democratic left wing, enabled Prime Minister Hitoshi Ashida to form a cabinet of six Democrats, eight Social Democrats and two People's Cooperative members.
The Liberal Party and minor groups formed the Democratic Liberal Party on 15 March, the largest Diet group, with 153 members in the House of Representatives and 44 in the House of Councillors.

The new Police Reorganization Law decentralizing police administration took effect 7 March, and autonomous police forces were set up in all 1,605 municipalities with populations over 5,000; the shokutaku system was abolished on 31 March.

Purge screening: of 674,579 persons examined, 4,861 were removed from office and 2,816 barred; 165 of 1,424 information-media executives were barred; public-office screening committees were to end on 10 May.

The Second National Diet reconvened on 20 March; Ashida gave his administrative address and Economic Stabilization Board head Kuroki outlined economic policy, followed by interpellations on 22-25 March.
In the International Prosecution Section the defense summation ran from 2 to 31 March, arguing that ex-post-facto penalization of Japanese leaders might be seen as a gross injustice.

Labor disputes included coal-miner wage demands, a mediated settlement accepted 25 March by the electric power union, an express company union award on 9 March, and the arrest of 13 union officials at the Aikodo Printing Company.
Bank of Japan notes outstanding reached 218,775,000,000 yen on 31 March; Reconstruction Finance Bank loans totaled 54,439,200,000 yen on 29 February; February land sales to tenants were 61,857 cho.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover for Summation No. 30 (March 1948), table of contents by part and section, and lists of charts, maps and graphs (94 items) and the map of Japan.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Digest of the month: no organizational change in SCAP, formation of the Ashida cabinet, police reform, purge figures, war crimes trials, plus economic and social highlights.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: Reports that there was no change in the non-military organization of General Headquarters, SCAP, during March.

sections.title: Section 2. Political Activities
sections.summary: Summary of the Ashida coalition cabinet, 7 March police law, Democratic Liberal Party's 153 House seats, Diet reconvening 20 March, purge totals, crime figures and war crimes trials.

sections.title: Section 3. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Digest of production indexes and sector reports on natural resources, industry, labor, trade, rationing, finance, property control and science and technology for February-March.

sections.title: Section 4. Social Activities
sections.summary: Digest of public health, welfare, education, religion and media developments, including the model health center and communicable disease reports.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Detailed account of the Ashida cabinet formation, parties, Diet, purge, police and prison statistics, Japanese courts and the war crimes trials, including the Tokyo tribunal's defense summation.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Narrates cabinet formation under Ashida, hoarded goods, budgets, police reorganization, party realignment, the Diet session and the winding up of the purge committees.

sections.title: Political Developments: Formation of New Cabinet
sections.summary: Three-party policy agreement, left-wing Social Democratic reaction, cabinet membership, the Prime Minister's statement and ministers' policy statements with biographical sketches.

sections.title: Hoarded Goods
sections.summary: Large stocks of concealed goods uncovered, prosecution of a Diet member, a conference of procurators and an inventory order.

sections.title: National Government
sections.summary: Cabinet agreement on 1948-49 budgets, passage of three supplementary budgets, the new police system of 7 March and abolition of the shokutaku system.

sections.title: Political Parties
sections.summary: Positions of the Democratic, Social Democratic, People's Cooperative, Liberal, Social Renovation and Communist parties and the Green Breeze Society; Democratic Liberal Party formed 15 March.

sections.title: The Diet
sections.summary: Ashida's administrative address, party comments, interpellations by Saito, Asanuma and Itaya, Director General Kuroki's economic address and bills enacted and introduced.

sections.title: The Purge
sections.summary: Public office and information media screening results, loss of records and discontinuance of the purge committees by 10 May.

sections.title: Section 2. Public Safety
sections.summary: Black-market and crime reports, police reorganization, 146,669 offenses and 76,802 arrests in January, and 83,872 prisoners on 29 February.

sections.title: Section 3. Legal Affairs and War Crimes
sections.summary: Supreme Court caseload, 78 atrocity investigations, 12 trials of 73 suspects, and the Tokyo tribunal summations on Shiratori, Suzuki, Togo, Tojo, Umezu and defense of Hata, Doihara and Hiranuma.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Sector reports with statistics on agriculture, mining, industry, textiles, transport, communications, labor, trade, rationing, finance, property control and science for February-March 1948.

sections.title: Section 1. Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: Land sales to tenants of 61,857 cho in February (cumulative 280,763 cho), plus livestock slaughter, sericulture, marine landings, fishing petroleum allocations and whaling.

sections.title: Section 2. Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: February log production of 71,133,700 cubic feet, firewood and charcoal output, coal production and deliveries, crude oil drilling and mine production.

sections.title: Section 3. Heavy Industries
sections.summary: February coke output of 192,570 metric tons, iron and steel, nonferrous rolling, cement, shipbuilding, chemicals, machine tools, industrial machinery and rolling stock.

sections.title: Section 4. Manufacturing
sections.summary: Pulp and paper, glass, optical instruments, electrical goods, agricultural implements, handicrafts and miscellaneous goods; processed food reports unavailable after reporting shifted to government statistics.

sections.title: Section 5. Textile Industries
sections.summary: Cotton fabric output at a postwar high, raw silk back to December level, rayon increases, and wool, bast fiber, knit goods and clothing supply and stock tables.

sections.title: Section 6. Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: 156,740 registered commercial vehicles in February, rail traffic indexes, water-borne cargo, air transport, and electric energy and gas generation and consumption.

sections.title: Section 7. Communications
sections.summary: Ministry of Communications administration and contract bidding, wire and radio services, postal services, construction, equipment production, personnel and finances.

sections.title: Section 8. Labor
sections.summary: Kanju Kato named Labor Minister; union membership, coal, electric power and express-company wage disputes, Aikodo Printing production-control case, wages and employment.

sections.title: Section 9. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: January private trade approvals of 21 import contracts ($1,838,395) and 839 export contracts ($6,050,598), with trade by country, balances and commodities.

sections.title: Section 10. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Staple crop collection quota exceeded by 0.9 percent, rice stocks near 3,000,000 tons, producers' and consumers' goods, consumer price index and ten rationed commodities.

sections.title: Section 11. Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Japan notes at 218,775,000,000 yen on 31 March, banks, deposit bureau, Reconstruction Finance Bank loans of 54,439,200,000 yen, securities liquidation and the budget.

sections.title: Section 12. Property Control and Reparations
sections.summary: Looted property worth 436,000 yen reported, restitution of 35,000 yen, looted ships, antitrust and cartel actions, and reparations.

sections.title: Section 13. Science and Technology
sections.summary: Renewal Committee for the Organization of Science met 23-24 February; research activities, personnel, patents and standards, and publications.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health, welfare, education, religion and media reports, with a model health center opened 15 March, repatriation, vital statistics and SCAP information libraries.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Model Health Center opened in Tokyo 15 March; communicable diseases, medical supplies, narcotics, public assistance, LARA relief, repatriation and vital statistics.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Religion, Cultural Resources and Media of Expression
sections.summary: Teacher salary study, conferences for teachers, Catholic church statistics, national treasures, press, radio, films, theater, music and SCAP libraries with 48,729 visits; ends with map page.
